retrieved_sources.title: Configuration Guide for ArtifactService Artifacts Deployment
retrieved_sources.text:
**What is a workload.yaml?**

* Workload yaml specifies a list of custom artifact versions to be used during PipelineHub CD.
* Based on the specifications in this file, either fixed versions or rules to select latest versions for a given release are used to create the CI/CD service version which gets deployed to the configured POD.
* You can specify any of the following artifact types supported by CloudNative Platform: workloadArtifacts, genericArtifacts and signalHandlers
* The workload yaml file needs to be in the **main** branch of your deployment config repo.
* PipelineHub first checks for existence of the file in the main branch and if does not exist, fallsback to the file's presence in the master branch.

retrieved_sources.title: ConfigurePipeline Java Microservices Skill
retrieved_sources.text:
The skill supports Java microservices only (Build phase). 

It creates or validates:

* `.pipeline_dep.yml` at the repository root when the source repository contains more than one microservice
* `.pipeline_pipeline.yml` per microservice
* `scqs_scan_jenkins.properties` per microservice
* `pipeline-container-config.yml` per microservice

Install the Skill
-----------------

### Prerequisites

Access : 

* Access to the [ReleaseEngineering skills repository](https://git.example.com/reference/resource-220).
* PipelineHub project onboarding access is required later if you intend to create or update the PipelineHub project after generating the files.

Tooling : 

* Codex desktop application or Codex CLI.
* Git.
* Python 3  (Python 3 runs the bundled Pipelineization generator. It scans the Java source repository and its Helm configuration, then creates the required Pipeline-related CI/CD files and configuration for each microservice. Python is not a dependency of the Java application itself.

retrieved_sources.title: LowCode CI-CD Onboarding
retrieved_sources.text:
1. Publishing LowCode artifacts to CloudNative Platform: PipelineHub publishes the DBBOM generated in CI pipeline to CloudNative Platform, with artifact version being the release version of the CI pipeline
2. Creating CloudNative service version: PipelineHub creates a CloudNative service version (unpublished, used for CICD purposes only) containing LowCode artifacts from step 1
	1. You can choose the base CloudNative service version as the basis
	2. If you choose the base to be "Latest Regular Service Version", PipelineHub uses the latest service version in the CloudNative repo and artifact, and plugs in the LowCode artifacts
	3. If you choose the base to be "Workload YAML", PipelineHub uses the workload yaml file in your deployment repo, and plugs in the LowCode artifacts
	4. To configure a workload yaml in the deployment repo, see the instructions below
3. Creating Patch Bundle: PipelineHub creates a patch bundle containing the CloudNative service version created in step 2
4. Patch to the POD: PipelineHub uses ApplicationPatchBundle patching to patch the patch bundle in step 3 to the POD
	1. Please see the instructions below on how to monitor patching job
